principles.text: Validation means money: people saying they would pay doesn't mean they will. Put a buy button on it.
Take a proven idea and make one part of it 10x better; a proven idea moves the risk from demand to execution.
Solve cash flow first with a job or an agency; service income gives you validation and runway to build.
Distribution matters, monetization matters from day one, and build painkillers, not vitamins.
Focus on the 20% of work with 80% of the impact; most of the time that's the boring stuff.

sampleQA.question: How do I validate an idea before building it?

answer.text: Find a product already making money and make one part of it 10x better, so your risk is execution, not demand.
Sell it as a service first to test demand and fund the build, then turn it into a product.
Put a buy button on a landing page. Stated interest isn't demand; paying customers are.
Pick a narrow ideal customer and write the page to that one person; building for everyone means nobody loves it.

sampleQA.question: What's the playbook for growing on X as a founder?

answer.text: Fix your profile first: real face photo, short bio, and a pinned post with your goal and story.
Rotate four content types: entertaining, educational, inspirational and convincing. Entertainment warms up reach for the rest.
Copy the concept behind top posts in your niche, not the post. Track everything, double down on winners, kill what doesn't work.
Post wins and losses honestly; struggles resonate most and turn into inbound clients.

sampleQA.question: How does a new product with no domain authority get found in Google and AI search?

answer.text: Target LLM retrieval and borrow the authority of LinkedIn and YouTube instead of relying on your own new site.
Start with versus, alternatives and review pages about competitors, and interlink them.
Draft with AI, then edit by hand to add first-party data and firsthand experience, in short digestible paragraphs.
